title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Zambia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Zambia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Zambia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: Managing post-death administrative, probate, social security, tax, and consular formalities in Zambia centers on civil death registration under Cap. 51, estate administration through the High Court or Administrator-General, survivor and funeral benefit claims, and consular document legalization. Because the Zambia Revenue Authority (zra.org.zm) and Foreign Affairs (mofaic.gov.zm) portals encounter external TLS certificate errors and NAPSA public web pages apply automated firewall blocks externally, this guide cites live DNRPC, Judiciary of Zambia, PSPF, NHIMA, CRVS Laws Zambia, HCCH, and ZambiaLII statutory portals.

steps.title: Medical Certificate and Civil Death Registration (DNRPC)
steps.html:
• Obtain a Medical Certificate of Cause of Death from the attending physician or hospital before arranging burial permits [3].
  • Register the death in the district of occurrence with the Department of National Registration, Passport and Citizenship (DNRPC) under Section 18(1) of the Births and Deaths Registration Act (Cap. 51): on-time notification within 1 calendar month is free of charge, delayed notice with valid explanation runs up to 3 months, medical-certificate registration runs up to 12 months (Rule 34), and notices beyond 12 months require Registrar-General authorization (Rule 37) [1][2][3].

steps.title: Estate Probate, Intestate Succession, and Administrator-General
steps.html:
• Check whether a valid written will exists under the Wills and Administration of Testate Estates Act (Cap. 60) or whether intestate distribution applies under the Intestate Succession Act (Cap. 59) [6].
  • Apply through the High Court Probate Registry of the Judiciary of Zambia in Lusaka or provincial centres for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration (attaching the Death Certificate, Burial Permit, National Registration Card, Originating Summons, Affidavits, beneficiary consents, and Administration Bond), or coordinate with the Administrator-General under the Administrator-General's Act (Cap. 58) where applicable [6][7].

steps.title: NAPSA and PSPF Funeral Grants and Survivor Benefits
steps.html:
• Submit Funeral Grant and Survivors' Pension or Lump Sum claims under the National Pension Scheme Act, 1996 (Cap. 256) with the National Pension Scheme Authority (NAPSA) at regional offices or via member channels, as external automated visits to napsa.co.zm encounter firewall blocks [8].
  • For civil-service members, apply through the Public Service Pensions Fund (PSPF) under the Public Service Pensions Act No. 73 of 2026: death in service under 10 years triggers a special death gratuity plus refunded contributions with interest, 10 to 20 years triggers estate gratuity plus spouse and minor-child pensions, and 20 or more years triggers posthumous retirement rules under section 34 [4][5].
  • Notify the National Health Insurance Management Authority (NHIMA) regarding insured member updates [9].

steps.title: Financial Accounts and Property Transfer Tax Clearance
steps.html:
• Present certified Death Certificates and High Court Letters of Administration or Grant of Probate to Zambian banks and asset registries prior to account release or estate settlement [6].
  • Coordinate Property Transfer Tax (PTT) provisional returns and Tax Clearance Certificates directly with local Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) offices before registering estate real estate or share transfers [6].

steps.title: Cross-Border Consular Legalization (Non-Apostille)
steps.html:
• Zambia is not a Contracting Party to the HCCH 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, meaning Apostille stamps do not authenticate Zambian documents abroad [10].
  • Route Zambian Death Certificates and High Court probate grants through notarization and pre-certification by the Consular and Protocol Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (Charter House, Independence Avenue, Lusaka), followed by destination embassy legalization [10].

contacts.name: Department of National Registration, Passport and Citizenship (DNRPC)
contacts.note: Independence Avenue, Lusaka and provincial offices; death registration under Cap. 51 and civil certificates.

contacts.name: Judiciary of Zambia
contacts.note: Plot 438 Independence Avenue, Lusaka; High Court Probate Registry for Grant of Probate and Letters of Administration.

contacts.name: Public Service Pensions Fund (PSPF)
contacts.note: Pensions House, Sapele Road, Lusaka; death-in-service gratuities and survivor pensions under Act No. 73 of 2026.

contacts.name: National Pension Scheme Authority (NAPSA)
contacts.note: Administers National Pension Scheme Act Funeral Grants and Survivors' Benefits (visit regional branches due to external firewall gating on napsa.co.zm).

contacts.name: National Health Insurance Management Authority (NHIMA)
contacts.note: Stand No. 27396, Alick Nkhata Road, Longacres, Lusaka (+260 211 356 498); national health insurance records.
